notes: re-scoped from the shared unit to sysml alone (ADR-0015)
decision: SysML 8.2.2.18.3 states `'do' { kind = 'effect' } ownedRelatedElement += EffectBehaviorUsage`. The braced part assigns into the abstract syntax and contributes no token. The Xtext writes `kind = EffectFeatureKind ownedRelatedElement += EffectBehaviorUsage`, and EffectFeatureKind (SysML.xtext:1913) is an enum whose only literal is `effect = 'do'`, so the two accept the same keyword. The 'do' here is the effect of a transition and is not the same 'do' as a state's DoActionMember, which the same clause states separately over StateActionUsage; the two are told apart by where they appear, not by their keyword.

evidence.note: States the production; the rule is its transcription with the abstract-syntax assignment dropped.
Line 60 `do send new StartSignal() to controller` is the effect of the transition on lines 56-61: 'do' followed by an EffectBehaviorUsage taking its TransitionSendActionUsage form.
Second opinion. Same keyword, reached through the one-literal enum at 1913.
